questions.question: Describe classical conditioning and operant conditioning, using examples from psychological research.

points.text: Classical conditioning (Pavlov): learning by association. NS paired with UCS produces CR. Explains phobias (Little Albert - white rat paired with loud noise = fear of rat and similar objects). Operant conditioning (Skinner): learning by consequences. Positive reinforcement increases behaviour (rewards); punishment decreases it. Explains maintained behaviours (addiction, token economies).

questions.question: Explain Bandura's Social Learning Theory and evaluate how well it accounts for observational learning.

points.text: SLT: we learn by observing models. Process: Attention -> Retention -> Reproduction -> Motivation. Bandura's Bobo doll: children who observed aggressive models imitated aggression (67% of boys in aggressive condition vs 0% in control). Evaluation: explains learning without direct experience; includes cognitive processes; supported by research. Limitations: lab study (low ecological validity), Bobo

questions.question: Compare the behaviourist approach with the cognitive approach, evaluating their relative contributions.

points.text: Behaviourism: observable behaviour only, learning through conditioning, environmental determinism. Cognitive: internal mental processes, information processing, schemas. Behaviourism strengths: scientific (observable), practical applications (systematic desensitisation, token economies). Limitations: ignores thinking, machine-like, environmental determinism.
